command: mkpoc.py

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate fuzz-format input for libxml2 fuzz/xml.c target.

Format: [4-byte int opts] then pairs of (url-string, content-string).
Strings: bytes verbatim, terminated by backslash-newline ('\\\n');
a literal backslash inside is escaped as two backslashes.
The FIRST pair is the main document entity.
"""
import struct, sys

XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE = 1 << 10

def esc(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for b in s:
        if b == 0x5C:  # backslash
            out.append(0x5C)
        out.append(b)
    out += b"\\\n"
    return bytes(out)

def make(opts: int, pairs):
    data = struct.pack("<i", opts)
    for url, content in pairs:
        data += esc(url) + esc(content)
    return data

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import json
    spec = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
    opts = spec.get("opts", XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE)
    pairs = [(u.encode("latin1") if isinstance(u, str) else u,
              c.encode("latin1") if isinstance(c, str) else c)
             for (u, c) in spec["entities"]]
    open(spec["out"], "wb").write(make(opts, pairs))
    print("wrote", spec["out"], len(make(opts, pairs)), "bytes")

arguments.content: #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Generate a seed corpus (fuzz-format) of XInclude-heavy XML docs.""" import os, struct, sys, itertools OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "_work", "corpus") os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True) def esc(s: bytes) -> bytes: out = bytearray() for b in s: if b == 0x5C: out.append(0x5C) out.append(b) out += b"\\\n" return bytes(out) def fuzz_input(opts: int, pairs): data = struct.pack("' docs["three_sib"] = f'' docs["nested_elems"] = f'' docs["two_pairs_diffurl"] = f'' docs["root_inc"] = f'' docs["root_inc_pair"] = f'' docs["with_txt"] = f'premidpost' docs["in_attrs_env"] = f'' docs["last_child"] = f'text' docs["empty_txt"] = f'' docs["fallback"] = f'fb' docs["entity_subst"] = f']>&e;' docs["deep_chain"] = f'' + ''.join(f'' for i in range(20)) + '' + ''.join(f'' for i in reversed(range(20))) + '' # include near end of parse with different content afterwards docs["inc_then_big"] = f'' + 'x'*2000 + '' txtdoc = lambda inner: f'{inner}' # parse=xml includes whose target contains another include xmlres_with_inc = f'' for name, doc in docs.items(): for opts in OPT_SET: ent = [("doc.xml", doc), ("t.txt", "abc"), ("u.txt", "def")] if name == "empty_txt": ent = [("doc.xml", doc), ("e.txt", "")] if name == "fallback": ent = [("doc.xml", doc), ("t.txt", "abc")] if name == "in_attrs_env": ent = [("doc.xml", doc), ("t.txt", "abc")] data = fuzz_input(opts, ent) open(os.path.join(OUT, f"{name}_{opts:x}.bin"), "wb").write(data) # xml-parse include of an entity containing text include (nested processing) for opts in [XINC, XINC|NOENT]: for i, (outer, innerdoc) in enumerate([ (f'', xmlres_with_inc), (f'', f''), (f'', xmlres_with_inc), ]): data = fuzz_input(opts, [("doc.xml", outer), ("x.xml", innerdoc), ("t.txt", "abc")]) open(os.path.join(OUT, f"xmlnested{i}_{opts:x}.bin"), "wb").write(data) # absolute url variants for the reader (doc url irrelevant) for opts in [XINC]: data = fuzz_input(opts, [ ("http://m/doc.xml", f''), ("http://x/t.txt", "abc"), ]) open(os.path.join(OUT, f"absurl_{opts:x}.bin"), "wb").write(data) # misc: multiple entities of similar names for opts in [XINC]: data = fuzz_input(opts, [ ("doc.xml", f''), ("t.txt", "abc"), ]) open(os.path.join(OUT, f"mix_{opts:x}.bin"), "wb").write(data) print("seeds:", len(os.listdir(OUT)))

NEWS file for libxml2

v2.11.0: Apr 28 2023

### Major changes

Protection against entity expansion attacks, also known as "billion laughs"
has been greatly improved. Malicious files should be detected reliably now
and false positives should be reduced. It is possible though that large
documents which make heavy use of entities are rejected now.

This release finally fixes symbol visibility on UNIX systems. Internal
symbols will now be hidden. While these symbols were never declared in public
headers, it was still possible to declare them manually. Now this won't work.

All symbol information has been removed from the ELF version script to fix
link errors with --no-undefined-version. The version nodes are kept so it
should still be possible to run binaries linked against older versions.

About 90 memory errors in code paths handling malloc failures have been fixed.
While these issues shouldn't impact security, this improves robustness under
memory pressure.

The XInclude engine has been reworked to properly support nested includes.

Several cases of quadratic behavior in the XML push parser have been fixed.

Refactoring has begun on some buffering and encoding code with the goal of
simplifying this part of the code base and improving error reporting.

Other highlights:

- Consolidated private header files.
- Major rework of the autoconf build.
- Deprecated several outdated and internal functions.

Special thanks to Google's Open Source Security Subsidies program for
sponsoring much of the work on this release!

Ongoing work on libxml2 relies on funding. For a list of important open
issues see <https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/issues/507>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal git pack reader: find commit objects whose subject matches keywords,
and walk ancestry from a given commit."""
import struct, zlib, sys, os, glob, re

class GitPack:
    def __init__(self, packpath):
        self.packpath = packpath
        self.f = open(packpath, 'rb')
        magic = self.f.read(4)
        assert magic == b'PACK', magic
        ver, nobj = struct.unpack('>II', self.f.read(8))
        self.nobj = nobj
        # object offsets stored in the pack after header: first entry types are implicit;
        # we use the idx to map sha->offset instead.
    def read_obj_at(self, offset, cache):
        # returns (type, data)
        if offset in cache:
            return cache[offset]
        self.f.seek(offset)
        c = self.f.read(1)[0]
        type = (c >> 4) & 7
        size = c & 15
        shift = 4
        while c & 0x80:
            c = self.f.read(1)[0]
            size |= (c & 0x7f) << shift
            shift += 7
        if type == 6:  # OFS_DELTA
            c = self.f.read(1)[0]
            base_off = c & 0x7f
            while c & 0x80:
                c = self.f.read(1)[0]
                base_off = ((base_off + 1) << 7) | (c & 0x7f)
            base_off = offset - base_off
            data = zlib.decompress(self.f.read())
            base_type, base_data = self.read_obj_at(base_off, cache)
            data = self.apply_delta(base_data, data)
            cache[offset] = (base_type, data)
            return base_type, data
        elif type == 7:  # REF_DELTA
            base_sha = self.f.read(20)
            data = zlib.decompress(self.f.read())
            base_type, base_data = self.read_sha(base_sha, cache)
            data = self.apply_delta(base_data, data)
            cache[offset] = (base_type, data)
            return base_type, data
        else:
            data = zlib.decompress(self.f.read())
            cache[offset] = (type, data)
            return type, data
    def apply_delta(self, base, delta):
        out = bytearray()
        i = 0
        def read_varint():
            nonlocal i
            val = 0
            shift = 0
            while True:
                c = delta[i]; i += 1
                val |= (c & 0x7f) << shift
                shift += 7
                if not (c & 0x80):
                    return val
        base_size = read_varint()
        res_size = read_varint()
        assert base_size == len(base), (base_size, len(base))
        while i < len(delta):
            c = delta[i]; i += 1
            if c & 0x80:
                cp_off = 0; cp_size = 0
                if c & 0x01: cp_off = delta[i]; i += 1
                if c & 0x02: cp_off |= delta[i] << 8; i += 1
                if c & 0x04: cp_off |= delta[i] << 16; i += 1
                if c & 0x08: cp_off |= delta[i] << 24; i += 1
                if c & 0x10: cp_size = delta[i]; i += 1
                if c & 0x20: cp_size |= delta[i] << 8; i += 1
                if c & 0x40: cp_size |= delta[i] << 16; i += 1
                if cp_size == 0: cp_size = 0x10000
                out += base[cp_off:cp_off+cp_size]
            elif c:
                out += delta[i:i+c]; i += c
            else:
                raise ValueError('invalid delta op')
        assert len(out) == res_size
        return bytes(out)
    def read_sha(self, sha, cache):
        # find in same pack: scan via idx? we don't have idx here; try all offsets.
        # Instead do linear search by trying to read objects - very slow. Use idx map.
        raise NotImplementedError

class PackSet:
    def __init__(self, gitdir):
        self.gitdir = gitdir
        self.packs = []
        self.sha_to_pack = {}
        for idxpath in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(gitdir, 'objects', 'pack', '*.idx'))):
            packpath = idxpath[:-4] + '.pack'
            d = open(idxpath, 'rb').read()
            assert d[:4] == b'\xfftOc'
            ver = struct.unpack('>I', d[4:8])[0]
            n = struct.unpack('>I', d[8 + 255*4: 8 + 256*4])[0]
            # v2 layout: fanout(256*4) + shas(20*n) + crc(4*n) + offsets(4*n)
            off = 8 + 256*4
            shas = [d[off + 20*i: off + 20*(i+1)] for i in range(n)]
            off += 20*n
            # crc
            off += 4*n
            # offsets: 4 bytes each; MSB set => large offset table (8 bytes)
            offsets = []
            large = []
            off0 = off
            for i in range(n):
                v = struct.unpack('>I', d[off:off+4])[0]; off += 4
                if v & 0x80000000:
                    offsets.append(None); large.append(v & 0x7fffffff)
                else:
                    offsets.append(v)
            if large:
                off = off0 + 4*n
                for i in range(n):
                    if offsets[i] is None:
                        idx = large.pop(0)
                        # large offset table index
                        pass
            self.packs.append(packpath)
            for i, sha in enumerate(shas):
                self.sha_to_pack.setdefault(sha, []).append((packpath, offsets[i]))
        self.cache = {}
    def read(self, sha):
        if sha in self.cache:
            return self.cache[sha]
        entries = self.sha_to_pack.get(sha)
        if not entries:
            raise KeyError('missing object ' + sha.hex())
        for packpath, off in entries[:1]:
            p = GitPack(packpath)
            p.cache = self.cache
            return p.read_obj_at(off, self.cache)

def parse_commit(data):
    lines = data.split(b'\n')
    out = {'tree': None, 'parents': [], 'author': None, 'message': b''}
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines) and lines[i] != b'':
        line = lines[i]
        if line.startswith(b'tree '):
            out['tree'] = line[5:25]
        elif line.startswith(b'parent '):
            out['parents'].append(line[7:27])
        elif line.startswith(b'author '):
            out['author'] = line
        i += 1
    out['message'] = b'\n'.join(lines[i+1:])
    return out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    gitdir = sys.argv[1]
    start = sys.argv[2]
    pat = re.compile(sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 'xinclude|reader|use.after.free|UAF', re.I)
    ps = PackSet(gitdir)
    # BFS backwards/forwards via parents until root; search messages.
    seen = set()
    stack = [bytes.fromhex(start)]
    found = []
    count = 0
    while stack and count < 200000:
        sha = stack.pop()
        if sha in seen: continue
        seen.add(sha)
        try:
            typ, data = ps.read(sha)
        except KeyError:
            continue
        if typ != 1:  # commit
            continue
        count += 1
        cm = parse_commit(data)
        msg = cm['message'].decode('utf-8', 'replace')
        first = msg.split('\n')[0]
        if pat.search(msg):
            found.append((sha.hex(), first, msg[:300]))
        for p in cm['parents']:
            stack.append(p)
    print('scanned', count, 'commits, matched', len(found))
    for sha, first, msg in found[:60]:
        print(sha, '|', first)
